Anya (eng-runtime): Heads up — perf-bot flagged a small regression after rolling the latest kernel selector change. p99 latency up ~+3% on long-context H100 runs.
perf-bot: regression detected for model:gptx-large on pool:h100; p99 +3.2%, mean +0.6. details: https://perf/reports/174999
Mike (eng-runtime): seeing this locally too. Traces point to more KV cache fragmentation and some fallback to the generic GEMM kernel during generation.
Cheng (kernel): interesting — the selector heuristics now prefer kernel_v2 for shorter sequences but the fallback threshold is too aggressive when KV pages are fragmented. v2 has worse tail for long prefixes.
Sarah (perf-bench): I ran the 8k seq suite across A100/H100/L4 last night. Pattern: H100 p99 regressed, A100 small bump, L4 unchanged. Token packing counts are higher on H100 which may trigger different kernel path.
Raul (eng-infra): config we rolled: `
{
  "kernel_selector": "auto_v2",
  "kv_fragment_aware": true,
  "batching": {
    "max_tokens_per_batch": 65536
  }
}`
looks like the frag-aware toggle interacts poorly with the per-device ceil.
Anya (eng-runtime): Proposed quick mitigation: cap `max_tokens_per_batch` per GPU (lower for H100/A100 when long-context workload detected) and add a kv_fragment penalty in queue score so fragmented slices are less likely to pack aggressively.
Cheng (kernel): agree. Suggested per-GPU defaults (start conservative): `A10: 48k`, `T4: 32k`, `L4: 40k`, `A100: 56k`, `H100: 48k`. These are tokens-per-batch not batch-size.
Sarah (perf-bench): I'll run a sweep tomorrow across those caps + two queue policy variants: `kv_penalty = 0.1` and `kv_penalty = 0.25`. Expect to see reduced p99 but potential throughput loss.
Mike (eng-runtime): also let's add telemetry: tag requests that hit the kv-frag penalty and emit `pack_decision` events so we can correlate kernel choice and fragment hits.
Anya (eng-runtime): quick patch in prod to test: set H100/A100 caps and kv_penalty=0.1 for 2h canary on a subset of traffic. If p99 drops back to baseline we widen. Who can own the canary?
Raul (eng-infra): I can deploy canary toggles and route 5% traffic to it. Will add alert if overall p99 changes >1.5%.
Cheng (kernel): one more note — we should make kernel fallback deterministic for the same KV layout to avoid jitter. I'll open a tiny PR to stabilize selector decisions (prefer same kernel across similar fragment counts).
Sarah (perf-bench): test matrix I'll run: `
- GPUs: H100, A100, L4, A10, T4
- Caps: default vs per-gpu caps
- kv_penalty: 0, 0.1, 0.25
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, pack_rate, kernel_switch_rate, fragment_hits`
Mike (eng-runtime): sounds good. If fragment_hits drop and kernel_switch_rate drops, we win.
Anya (eng-runtime): OK team — next steps: Raúl deploys canary, Sarah runs sweep and posts results, Cheng lands deterministic selector PR, Mike adds telemetry. Re-check in ~3h. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: created alert runbook #174999-canary-rollback; notified eng-oncall.
